Subject: Initial redlines: Order Form + data role carveouts

Hi Dana,

Thanks again for the sync earlier — attaching the latest order form with our proposed legal redlines and a short DPA summary sheet that highlights where we expect friction. Two specific areas Helixa raised on the call: (1) processor/processor-of-processor expectations for the EU workload, and (2) the export-route language if you need us to host in a specific EU region or route exports to a partner.

Quick ask from our side: can you review the two redline sections I flagged on pages 2 and 6 and confirm whether Helixa can accept (A) our suggested processor-role split, which keeps most subprocessor liability with Redwood but accepts a narrow processor-of-processor carveout for vendor-managed telemetry, or (B) your team’s proposed equal-liability language? If neither, please provide an alternate sentence we can propose to execs.

            DPA_ProcessorRoles_Options.xlsx (spreadsheet)

- Legal check on your suggested alternate language by EOD tomorrow (Wed 9th)

From: Dana Liu <dana.liu@helixa-systems.com>

Date: Wed, 09 Sep 2026 11:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Initial redlines: Order Form + data role carveouts

Ben —

Thanks for the materials, and for the clear summary. We reviewed the redlines with our procurement and external counsel. High-level: Helixa is comfortable with Redwood acting as processor for the hosted API product, but we need clearer guardrails where we’re explicitly routing EU customer data through Helixa-managed tooling (examples: telemetry exports, webhook delivery).

Two asks from our counsel:
1) Processor roles: replace the blanket processor-of-processor carveout with a short, scoped clause: "Where customer data is exported to a Helixa-managed integration (identified in Exhibit B), Helixa shall act as a processor for that integration only, subject to the security controls in Exhibit B." This limits the scope and ties to an exhibit to be populated post-signature.

2) SCCs/Export route: the EU SCCs template is fine, but we need explicit language in the order form confirming the routing priority: (i) EU-hosted region; (ii) Helixa designated partner region; (iii) fallback to Redwood multi-region. If an EU-hosted region is required, Helixa will cover any incremental hosting surcharge; we just need a process to request that routing change and an SLA for the change window.

Finally, Helixa’s security team requests a short evidence package for the SCCs check: SOC 2 scope summary, KMS key custody notes, and a subprocessor list. If Redwood can provide a redacted subprocessor list (names + region + purpose), that will speed internal approval.

I can be on the redlines call Thu morning; Sam will take procurement-level notes.

Best,
Dana Liu
Head of Legal Operations | Helixa Systems
Dana.Liu@helixa-systems.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dana Liu <dana.liu@helixa-systems.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial redlines: Order Form + data role carveouts

Dana / Ben —

Appreciate the clear asks. I reviewed Helixa’s suggested scoped language and SCC routing priority. Below are legal tradeoffs and a practical path to execution that I think will get both legal teams to signoff quickly.

1) Processor-of-processor carveout (proposed solution)
Option A (preferred, low friction): Use Helixa’s scoped clause but add two short guards: (i) the integration list is maintained in Exhibit B and may be updated by mutual written consent; (ii) Redwood retains responsibility for security obligations under the DPA for all subprocessor activity where Redwood selected the subprocessor. Suggested sentence: "For integrations identified in Exhibit B where Helixa configures and operates the integration, Helixa shall act as Processor for that integration only, provided that Redwood remains responsible for Redwood-selected subprocessors and for ensuring that any Helixa-selected subprocessors maintain equivalent safeguards."

Rationale: preserves Helixa’s ask for scope while limiting open-ended liability.

2) SCCs + Export routing (practical execution)
Proposal: Add routing priority language to the order form and operationalize via a simple Routing Request process in the Console (HubSpot ticket or support API). We will include:
- Priority text copied into the Order Form (EU region requested in writing + estimated lead time)
- An incremental hosting surcharge line item in the Order Form (TBD commercial signoff)
- SLA: 10 business days standard, expedited 3 business days for a premium fee

3) Evidence package (what we can provide now)
We can produce: SOC 2 summary (scoping doc), redacted subprocessor list (name + region + purpose), and a KMS custody description (no keys). I will ask Security to produce a 1-page bundle. Can Helixa confirm the minimum redaction level acceptable?

4) Next steps and call prep - I support the scoped Exhibit B approach (Option A) — please confirm if Helixa’s counsel accepts the added Redwood responsibility sentence above.
- If Helixa wants the broader equal-liability language, escalate to our GC for sign-off; that will add ~72 hours.
- Ben: please schedule a 30-minute touch on Thu 10:30am PT / 19:30 CET (or suggest alternate). I’ll bring the Option A language as a one-paragraph amendment for quick review.
